learning_outcomes.text: Determine stresses and strains in an elastic continuum.
Assess modes of failure for components under bending and torsional loading.
Analyse dynamic behaviour of systems with one-degree-of-freedom by applying the notions of stiffness, damping, natural frequency and rate decay.
Determine equivalent models for rigid body systems, analyse and evaluate their dynamic behaviour by using notions of experimental dynamics.

syllabus_topics: Continuum Stress Analysis: Elasticity of a continuum.
Use of strain gauges to determine strains in loaded components.
Application of thin wall pressure vessel theory.
Application of Rankine, Tresca and Von-Mises theories to components under bending and torsional loading conditions.
Application to brittle and ductile materials.
Use of Euler, Rankine-Gordon and Perry-Robertson methods.
Factors affecting the endurance limit and their application.
Dynamics and Vibration 1: Free vibration of one-degree-of-freedom systems, modelling, equation of motion, harmonic motion and spectral analysis.
Dynamics and Vibration 2: Forced vibration of damped and undamped systems, time and frequency response, natural frequencies and modes, notions of experimental dynamics.
